title: How to choose an incentive platform for sending rewards at scale
summary: Choosing an incentive platform? Learn what features matter, how pricing works, and get advice on how to find the right one for your business.
body_markdown:
Sending rewards manually typically looks something like this: buying gift cards in batches, chasing down recipient info, and tracking everything in a spreadsheet. Then the support requests start rolling in. A gift card code doesn’t work, or a recipient says they never got it. And when finance asks for budget or tax information, you’re tabbing through countless documents and receipts to piece it together.


As reward volume grows, a manual approach gets harder to keep up with. That’s when the search for a dedicated incentive platform usually starts. Here’s what to look for in a platform that can help you scale your program.


## Key takeaways


-


**An incentive platform centralizes reward selection, delivery, tracking, and reporting in one system.** It makes it easier for businesses to send rewards at scale and offers a better redemption experience for recipients.


-


**Reward choice and local relevance matter.** Opt for a platform that lets recipients choose what they want, with a broad catalog of options that are relevant and available in the countries where they live.


-


**The right platform should make higher send volumes more manageable.** Batch uploads, scheduled sends, and integrations that automate reward delivery can save your team hours of admin work.


-


**Prioritize features that protect your budget.** Approval workflows, spending caps, and role-based permissions guard against internal mistakes. Fraud prevention tools catch external bad actors.


-


**Pricing may include platform fees, per-send fees, or reward markups.** These add up differently at scale, so be sure to weigh them against your expected volume.


## What is an incentive platform?


An **incentive platform** is software that helps businesses send, manage, and track rewards and payouts from one centralized system.


In many platforms, recipients can choose their own reward from a catalog and redeem it themselves. Delivery status and spend are tracked in one place, making reporting and performance monitoring easier for teams.


Some platforms go beyond basic sending and tracking with additional capabilities such as automated reward delivery, tax reporting, global coverage, and built-in fraud prevention.


## Who uses incentive platforms?


Incentive platforms support a wide range of teams and payout programs. Common use cases include:


-


**Researchers** compensating people for participating in surveys, interviews, clinical trials, and other studies. They need a platform that integrates with their survey tools, handles tax collection, and offers global rewards for international studies. Research firm[Forsta sent $2 million in incentives](https://www.tremendous.com/case-studies/tremendous-helps-forsta-send-2-million-in-research-incentives-in-100-countries/) to participants in more than 100 countries this way.


-


**Marketers** running loyalty programs, rebates, customer referrals, affiliate payouts, and other campaigns where rewards go out automatically once someone qualifies. A platform with API access or integrations with a CRM or other tools helps automate that process and reduce manual work.


-


**HR teams** sending rewards for employee recognition, such as spot bonuses or milestone achievements like work anniversaries. They need a simple way to distribute rewards in bulk across teams while maintaining visibility into spend and activity.


-


**Sales teams** paying out[sales performance incentive funds (SPIFFs)](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/spiff-program/) , channel partner rewards, and rep performance bonuses. They turn to a platform to deliver rewards quickly and track activity by program and individual rep.


-


**Product and technical teams**[embedding payouts directly into their own apps](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/embedded-reward-payments-guide/) , whether that’s a consumer platform rewarding users for completing tasks or a marketplace paying out earnings. They need flexible APIs, reliable infrastructure, sandbox environments, and fraud detection that holds up at high reward volumes.


## **How an incentive platform works**


Most platforms follow the same basic workflow for ordering and sending rewards:


1.


**Set program rules.** Define who gets rewarded, for what, and how much. Some platforms support custom rules, like reward tiers based on recipient behavior, or manager sign-off for amounts over $100.


2.


**Choose reward types.** Decide what to offer and[how much choice recipients get](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/should-recipients-choose-their-own-rewards/) . In some cases, you might pick a single reward for everyone, while for others it makes more sense to open up the full catalog and let recipients choose what they want.


3.


**Add recipients.** Upload a CSV file or connect the platform to your existing tech stack so rewards go out automatically. Most offer direct integrations with CRM, survey software, HRIS, and other common tools. Or build a custom workflow through[an API](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/how-do-gift-card-apis-work/) .


4.


**Send rewards and manage fulfillment.** Platforms typically deliver rewards by[email or SMS](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/email-vs-sms-gift-card-delivery/) with a link to claim them. Some also handle reward resends, as well as language localization and currency conversion for international recipients.


5.


**Track activity and reconcile spend.** Monitor delivery status, redemption activity, and spend through a single dashboard.

## **The key capabilities that matter for an incentive platform**


Incentive platforms can all start to look similar in a comparison grid. These are the capabilities to ask about in your evaluation.


### Reward variety


A broad catalog gives recipients a better chance of finding something they’ll actually use. Look for a platform that offers gift cards from popular brands alongside prepaid cards and monetary options like PayPal, Venmo, and bank transfers.


If you go with just a[gift card distributor](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/gift-card-distribution/#what-is-a-gift-card-distributor) , you’ll be left juggling multiple vendors if you want to introduce other kinds of reward options.


### Global coverage


[Sending rewards across borders](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/sending-global-payouts/) comes with added complexity. Check that a platform offers locally relevant rewards in the countries where your recipients live. A gift card to a retailer that doesn’t exist in someone’s country isn’t worth much. Bank transfer and digital wallet preferences vary widely by region, too.


A global incentive platform should also handle currency conversion and language localization, so recipients see the value in their own currency and can follow the redemption instructions without needing to translate anything.


### **Bulk sending and automated workflows**


Sending 10 rewards manually is manageable. Sending hundreds can quickly turn into a full-time job. Confirm that a platform allows for[batch uploads](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/sending-gift-cards-to-mulitple-people/) , scheduled sends, and automated triggers based on events in your other systems. It’s the difference between spending minutes managing your program and spending hours.


### **Centralized controls**


Every rewards program needs guardrails, especially if you have automations set up. Without them, one well-intentioned team member can accidentally burn through a quarterly budget in a week. Common controls include:


-


Approval workflows for high-value or sensitive sends


-


Spending caps by user, team, or program


-


Role-based permissions that dictate who can access what


### **Integrations and API access**


A platform should connect to the tools you already use. This is especially important if you want to send trigger-based rewards, since those workflows rely on data from your existing systems.


Teams that need custom workflows will want a strong integration library, API access, or both. If you’re embedding rewards into your own product, API quality matters even more. Prioritize an API that’s well-maintained and simple for developers to implement.


### **Reporting and tax documentation**


A real-time reporting dashboard should show reward activity and spend broken down by program, team, and individual sender. Exportable reports and tax documentation matter, too. Your finance team will likely need this information, and[some platforms even automate W-9 collection](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/automating-w9-collection/) and 1099 prep for U.S. recipients.


### **Security**


Reward programs carry real monetary value,[which makes them popular targets for fraudsters](https://www.tremendous.com/blog/how-to-prevent-incentives-fraud/) . An incentive platform should offer basic protections like single-use links, expiration settings, and SOC 2 compliance.


More robust platforms also offer fraud detection tools that flag suspicious activity before a reward goes out, not after your budget is gone. This could look like duplicate IP addresses or a dozen recipients cashing out to the same PayPal address.


### **Recipient experience**


The point of a reward is to make someone feel valued, whether it's a research participant, a loyal customer, or an employee. A clunky redemption process with too many clicks, confusing instructions, or limited payout options undermines that.


Choose a platform that makes rewards easy to claim and use, with clear instructions and dedicated support when something goes wrong.


## **Incentive platform costs and pricing models**


Incentive platforms are typically priced in three main ways:


-


**Platform fees:** A monthly or annual subscription for access


-


**Per-send fees:** A charge for each reward delivered


-


**Reward markup:** A percentage added to the face value of each reward


Some platforms combine these models. Others, like[Tremendous](https://www.tremendous.com/pricing/) , are entirely free to use.


When comparing pricing, calculate the total cost for your expected volume. A platform with no monthly fee but high per-send costs might be more expensive at scale than one with a flat subscription. Ask about hidden costs, too, like fees associated with currency conversion, funding a balance by bank transfer, or custom branding.


The right platform should make sending rewards feel effortless for you *and* your recipients. If your current process involves spreadsheets, multiple logins, or frequent " *where's my reward?* " emails, it's time to upgrade.
